name: Nanta Tech Ltd
title: Nanta Tech Ltd - 544668 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Nanta Tech's H2 FY26 margin jump (EBITDA 17.3%) and 52% H2 growth coincide with rising working capital and receivables, with FY27 guidance of ~40-50% revenue growth lacking supply-side evidence.

triggers.quote: because we already supplied and we did not raise our invoices because the commissioning is not happening

triggers.label: FY27 revenue growth 40-50%
triggers.quote: Growth, we are expecting to do around 40% to 50% growth in terms of overall operations revenues.

we are going to grow from dealer distribution network of four people right now to 15 and before FY27 end.

Margin lifted by IPO-funded push of projects into Q4

summary.headline: Nanta Tech H2 FY26 revenue rose 52.2% YoY to INR48.6 crores, with EBITDA margin up 580 bps to 17.3%.
summary.overview: H2 FY26 revenue from operations grew 52.2% YoY to INR48.6 crores, with EBITDA of INR8.4 crores (up 122.3%) and PAT of INR6 crores (up 124.3%). For FY26, revenue was INR70.1 crores (up 36.8%), EBITDA INR11.5 crores (margin 16.4%) and PAT INR8.2 crores (margin 11.7%). Management attributed the margin gain to a shift toward Robotics and AI, which it says earns higher EBITDA than AV. Working capital and receivables rose sharply in H2 because project billing and commissioning slipped at customers, and management expects working capital days to decline.

financial_highlights.change: +52.2% YoY vs INR31.9 crores in H2 FY25
+70.5% YoY vs INR4.7 crores; margin 11.7%, +260 bps

financial_highlights.metric: Robotics and AI share of FY26 revenue

segments.name: Robotics and AI (Albotix brand)
segments.commentary: Sold roughly 400 robots in FY26 across hospitality, manufacturing and government. Management cites hardware EBITDA margin of 20% to 25%, and about 30% for AMC and AI software. Contributed 36% to 37% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Audio-Visual (AV)
segments.commentary: Project-based end-to-end SITC (supply, installation, testing, commissioning) business for enterprise, institutional and government clients. Management says its EBITDA margin is lower than Robotics and AI, and it is the main driver of working capital build-up.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at around 40% to 50% (50% in one answer).
FY27 EBITDA guided to rise 2% to 3%, with EBITDA margin expected to rise in line with the Robotics and AI mix.
Robotics and AI targeted to reach about 60% to 65% of revenue, with the rest from AV and products.
UAE subsidiary targeted at about USD 2 million (around INR30 crores) of business in FY27, with revenue expected from Q2 FY27.
RSVP acquisition expected to bring INR15 crores to INR20 crores of business from RSVP's existing clients in FY27.
R&D spend via TRN expected at INR2 crores to INR3 crores in FY27, up from INR35 lakh to INR40 lakh last year; management says it is already in the plan.
Working capital days expected to decline, though not sharply.
capex_capacity: Experience Center, funded from IPO proceeds, about 95% complete; opening date to be announced soon.
IPO proceeds of about INR31.39 crores; roughly 99.5% utilised, with about INR15 lakh to INR20 lakh pending on material payments.
UAE subsidiary (Nanta Technologies FZ LLC) setup cost of INR20 lakh to INR25 lakh, covering office and licensing.
TRN (The Robotics Nexus) set up as a 51%-owned subsidiary for R&D in robotics, AI and automation.
Robots sourced mainly from third-party OEMs in India, with some models imported from China; no in-house manufacturing mentioned.
demand_pricing: Project-based AV business: customers are large contractors on 45 to 60 day credit terms; billing and commissioning delays pushed receivables up. Of about INR48 crores billed in H2, INR35 crores had been collected by the call, with more expected in June.
Robotics demand is led by hospitality (hotels, restaurants, hospitals, facility management). Management expects outdoor cleaning, reception and warehousing robots to grow in FY27.
Dealer and distributor network to grow from 4 to 15 by end FY27, across Mumbai, Bangalore, Delhi, Chennai and UAE, with a target-based incentive scheme (INR2 crores to INR10 crores targets).
GCC differentiation claimed through end-to-end hardware, software and integration, versus global peers.
Recent order: INR6.6 crores AI automation project from Pointer Insurance Broker (chatbot, predictive analytics, workflow automation).

qa_highlights.question: What drove the strong H2 performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 is seasonally strongest for project delivery (Q3 and Q4), and IPO funds helped pull projects into Q4 for delivery and billing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IPO fund utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR31.39 crores raised; nearly all used, with about 0.5% (INR15 lakh to INR20 lakh) pending on materials.

qa_highlights.question: Why did borrowings rise from INR50 lakh to about INR4 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly promoter loans, plus one bank loan at about 9.5% interest; the stated tenure was 8 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital days expand?
qa_highlights.answer: AV products were delivered, but invoices could not be raised until commissioning, because customer project completion was delayed; management expects this to ease.

qa_highlights.question: Are there overdue or stressed receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no overdue or sticky receivables, and the delay is in project completion and billing.

qa_highlights.question: What did the RSVP acquisition cost and contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition cost about INR98 lakh, closed late March 2026, with almost nil FY26 contribution; FY27 expected INR15 crores to INR20 crores from RSVP clients.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Robotics and AI share of revenue and the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: 36% to 37% in FY26, rising to about 60% to 65% over time; FY27 EBITDA guided up 2% to 3%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D spend and will it hit margins?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 R&D about INR35 lakh to INR40 lakh; FY27 planned at INR2 crores to INR3 crores via TRN, already included in the margin plan.

risks_watch: Working capital and receivables are elevated (debtors and unbilled work); collections of the remaining H2 receivables and June recoveries need tracking.
Project-based AV revenue depends on customer project timelines, which management says are often extended.
Guidance is internally inconsistent: 40% to 50% revenue growth against only 2% to 3% EBITDA growth implies margin compression, which is not reconciled on the call.
Robots are sourced from third-party OEMs and China imports; supply concentration and margin depend on partners.
Revenue concentration in Gujarat and the target of 15 dealers by FY27 are still to be proven.
UAE target of USD 2 million depends on first revenue in Q2 FY27 and on setup in a competitive GCC market.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and the Robotics and AI pivot, with specific targets for FY27. Cautious and vague on working capital, where the explanations were repeated, and on the EBITDA guidance, which was given in unclear terms during Q&A.
key_quotes: So, because of that reason, we are not able to raise the invoice and at the same time, our working capital get increased.
Robotics and AI are typically B2C kind of business where we are not involved into the large project execution kind of business.
We are expecting to grow around 50% in FY27.

adds.what: Experience Center (funded from IPO proceeds), opening date TBA
UAE subsidiary (Nanta Technologies FZ LLC) office and licensing setup, revenue expected from Q2 FY27

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 40-50% (midpoint 45%), backed by a specific UAE target of about USD 2 million (~INR30 crore), RSVP client business of INR15-20 crore, and dealer network expansion from 4 to 15, but no in-house capacity additions; robot supply is third-party sourced and FY27 EBITDA is guided only 2-3%.
